Describe the issue below: Class Weighting versus Amount Conditioning in Credit-Card Fraud Detection: A Dollar-Metric Study with a Temporal Explanation Audit Chenyu Wu Abstract Credit-card fraud losses are monetary, but papers often judge models with transaction-level scores. We ask whether transaction amount should shape training weights or be used later to order alerts. To separate this question from ordinary class imbalance handling, we keep total fraud-case weight fixed and vary only its allocation across fraud cases. Metrics are average precision, dollar recall, and dollar precision at fixed alert budgets over five seeds, with 95 percent day-block bootstrap intervals for the main contrasts.
